items.title: Three Ways Understanding Actually Dawns, and Three Grades of Bondage from Ordinary Being to Arhat

items.zh: 又有三種覺悟所知，能令三乘出離眾苦。一、從他聞音種類，二、內正思惟種類，三、長時修習止觀種類。又有三種覺悟所知。一者、具縛，二、不具縛，三、全無縛。
items.en: There are also three kinds of awakening to what is to be known, capable of freeing the three vehicles from the multitude of sufferings: first, the kind that comes from hearing another's voice; second, the kind that comes from correct inner reflection; third, the kind that comes from long cultivation of calm and insight. There are also three [degrees of] awakening to what is to be known: first, fully bound; second, not fully bound; third, entirely unbound.

items.title: Three Milestones on the Path, the Three Eyes That See Reality, and Three Ways to Defuse Affliction Before It Manifests

items.zh: 又有三種所應作事，修觀行者由此三事增上力故，修習信等一切善法。一者、永斷見道所斷諸煩惱已，證預流果；二者、永斷修道所斷諸煩惱已，漸次證得一來、不還、阿羅漢果；三者、證得阿羅漢已，現法樂住。又由三分照了一切所知境界增上力故，建立三眼。一者、肉眼，能照顯露無有障礙有見諸色；二者、天眼，能照顯露、不顯露、有障、無障有見諸色；三者、慧眼、照一切種若色非色所有諸法。又有三法，能害現行煩惱怨敵。一者、信順善友；二者、不與在家出家諸眾雜住；三者、內正作意，覺悟所知真實道理。
items.en: There are also three things to be accomplished, by whose power one who cultivates contemplation cultivates faith and all other wholesome qualities: first, having permanently severed the afflictions cut by the path of seeing, realising the fruit of stream-entry; second, having permanently severed the afflictions cut by the path of cultivation, gradually realising the fruits of once-return, non-return, and arhatship; third, having realised arhatship, abiding in the ease of the present life. By the power of three divisions illuminating every knowable object, three eyes are established: first, the physical eye, which illuminates visible matter that is exposed and unobstructed; second, the divine eye, which illuminates visible matter whether exposed or hidden, obstructed or unobstructed; third, the eye of wisdom, which illuminates all phenomena of every kind, whether possessing form or not. There are also three things capable of destroying the manifest enemy of affliction: first, trusting and following good friends; second, not dwelling intermixed with crowds of householders or renunciants; third, correct inner attention that awakens to the genuine principle of what is to be known.

items.title: Three Domains of Right Instruction, Three Ways to Rest Secure in Practice, and Three Grades of Mental One-Pointedness

items.zh: 復有三種正教誡方便，能展轉證後後所證及得涅槃。一、於尸羅正教誡方便，二、於心住正教誡方便，三、於覺悟所知真實道理正教誡方便。如正教誡方便有三種，當知數習正教誡方便亦爾。又於正教誡方便現修習時，由三種法得安隱住。一者、空、無願、無相、滅盡等至，二者、四靜慮，三者、四無量。又略有三種心一境性，能令證得如實智見。一、於意言中，種種差別所緣行相；二、意言無間，種種差別所緣行相；三、超度意言，專注一境，無種種無差別所緣行相。
items.en: There are also three kinds of correct instruction and admonition, by which one progressively realises each subsequent realisation and finally nirvāṇa: first, correct instruction and admonition regarding precepts; second, regarding settling the mind; third, regarding awakening to the genuine principle of what is to be known. As correct instruction and admonition has three kinds, know that its repeated cultivation likewise has three. Further, while actually cultivating correct instruction and admonition, one rests secure by three things: first, the attainments of emptiness, wishlessness, signlessness, and cessation; second, the four dhyānas; third, the four immeasurables. There are also, briefly, three kinds of one-pointedness of mind, capable of bringing about genuine knowledge and vision: first, the manifold and distinct aspect of the object within mental discourse; second, the manifold and distinct aspect of the object with mental discourse uninterrupted; third, the aspect of the object, without manifoldness or distinction, transcending mental discourse and focused single-pointedly.

items.title: Three Skilful Means for Reaching the Undecided, and What Genuine Purity and Genuine Sagehood Actually Consist In

items.zh: 又有三處，能善攝受於惡邪處妄計尊勝及處中庸所化有情，引入聖教。一、現己所有最勝神通，二、於他所有染淨諸行遮止開許；三、宣說妙法正教正誡。又有三淨，為欲斷除樂淨外道，以外事水暫除外垢，自謂已得第一清淨所起邪慢故；建立此三第一義淨。不淨處生超越因故。又有三種牟尼，為欲斷除持牟尼戒諸外道等暫息語言，自謂已得真實寂靜所起邪執故；又為顯說無倒牟尼故；建立三種真實牟尼。即是聖所愛戒所攝身語二業，及無漏心。
items.en: There are also three means capable of skilfully drawing in beings who falsely regard some evil, wrong position as supreme, as well as those of a genuinely undecided disposition, leading them into the sacred teaching: first, manifesting one's own supreme superknowledges; second, restraining or permitting others' defiled or pure conduct as appropriate; third, expounding the sublime Dharma through correct teaching and correct admonition. There are also three purities, established in order to eliminate the wrong conceit of ascetics who delight in purity through external means — using water to temporarily wash away outer defilement and claiming thereby to have attained the highest purity — these three ultimate purities are established because they are the actual cause of transcending rebirth in impure realms. There are also three [kinds of] sagely silence, established in order to eliminate the wrong grasping of ascetics who observe vows of silence and claim thereby to have attained genuine tranquility, and in order to reveal an undistorted sagely silence: these are precisely the bodily and verbal actions comprised within the precepts a noble one loves, together with the uncontaminated mind.

items.title: Overcoming Distracting Thought, the Three Unsurpassed Excellences, and the Three Knowledges That Cure Ignorance — the "Three Things" Category Closes

items.zh: 又有三法，能令處遠離者斷除現行不正尋思。謂由他所誹毀、自所誹毀、退失大利增上力故，所起愧、慚及與愛敬。又依道及道果，當知有三種最勝無上。謂無常智、苦智、無我智；樂速通等四種行跡；一切世間、出世間，有學、無學，時解脫、不動心解脫，最勝無上。修觀行者先得其智；由此智故，為斷煩惱，次修行跡；修行跡已，心得解脫。又有三明，當知為顯於前後中際，斷常二邊邪執現法涅槃愚癡沙門婆羅門無明性故，建立三明。
items.en: There are also three things that let one dwelling in seclusion sever manifest, unwholesome discursive thought: conscience arisen from the power of others' censure, shame arisen from the power of one's own self-censure, and reverent love arisen from the power of [seeing] the loss of great benefit. In dependence on the path and the fruit of the path, know there are three unsurpassed excellences: the knowledge of impermanence, of suffering, and of selflessness; the four courses of practice culminating in swift, blissful penetration; and every worldly and supramundane [attainment], the trainee's and the adept's, time-liberation and unshakeable-mind liberation. One who cultivates contemplation first attains this knowledge; by means of this knowledge, in order to sever affliction, one next cultivates the courses of practice; having cultivated the courses of practice, the mind attains liberation. There are also three knowledges. Know that these are established to reveal, with respect to the prior, later, and middle periods, the wrong grasping at the two extremes of permanence and annihilation, the delusion of a present-life nirvāṇa, and the very nature of ignorance among ascetics and brāhmins.

items.title: The Fourth Numeric Category Opens: The Four Foundations of Mindfulness, Comprehending All Knowledge and Countering All Bondage

items.zh: 已說三種佛教所應知處。次說四種。謂有四法，能攝一切所知及智。謂身，及聞思修增上念住以為依止緣身境慧。如身及緣身境慧，當知受、心、法，及緣受、心、法境慧亦爾。復有差別，謂四種縛。一、執取縛，二、領受縛，三、了別縛，四、執著縛。當知心於身，由執取縛所縛；於受，由內領受縛所縛；於色等境界相，由了別縛所縛；即於所說身等，由貪瞋等大小煩惱執著縛所縛。對治如是四種縛故，立四念住。
items.en: The three-thing category of what a Buddhist should know has now been explained. Next, the four-thing category. There are four phenomena that comprehend all that is knowable together with the knowing wisdom itself: namely, the body, and the wisdom born of hearing, reflection, and cultivation that, taking the foundation of mindfulness as its basis, takes the body as its object. As with the body and the wisdom that takes it as object, know that feeling, mind, and mental objects, and the wisdom that takes each as object, are likewise so. There is, further, a distinction: the four bonds. First, the bond of grasping; second, the bond of receiving; third, the bond of discriminating; fourth, the bond of attachment. Know that the mind is bound to the body by the bond of grasping; to feeling, by the bond of inward receiving; to the characteristic marks of form and other objects, by the bond of discriminating; and to the very body, feeling, and so forth just described, by the bond of attachment through greed, hatred, and the greater and lesser secondary afflictions. The four foundations of mindfulness are established precisely to counter these four bonds.

blocks.text: Today completes the threes and opens the fours with the **four foundations of mindfulness**, each the antidote to a particular way the mind is bound.

**Fully bound**, **not fully bound**, and **unbound**. Venerable Miào Jìng places an ordinary being who has attained the four dhyānas in the middle: "desire-realm craving is gone, though the afflictions of view remain." The arhat alone is unbound.

The **physical eye**, the **divine eye**, and the **wisdom eye** (Day 19). Master Cháng Bǎi on the limits of the first: it "sees near but not far, front but not back, inside but not outside, day but not night". The divine eye overcomes these limits; only the wisdom eye sees reality.

Three ways to rest secure in practice: the **heavenly** abidings (the four dhyānas), the **Brahmā** abidings (the four immeasurables), and the **noble** abidings (emptiness, wishlessness, signlessness, and cessation), as Venerable Miào Jìng lists them (Day 81). Master Cháng Bǎi and Venerable Miào Jìng differ on why an arhat still "abides in present ease": Venerable Miào Jìng notes that some reach arhatship in threshold concentration and then develop the dhyānas; Master Cháng Bǎi stresses enjoyment of the dhyānas as rest.

True sagehood (牟尼, *muni*, "silent one") is silence of body, speech, and mind, not the literal silence vow of certain ascetics, which, Venerable Miào Jìng notes, the passage is meant to correct. Real silence is the absence of wrongdoing.

From others' censure arises 愧; from one's own, 慚; from loss of benefit, reverent love (the *Pīxún jì*). Ru-Yi renders both as "shame"; the distinction between shame before others and conscience before oneself is worth keeping.
Three unsurpassed excellences, and the **three knowledges** (三明) that cure ignorance: recollection of past lives, knowledge of death and rebirth, and knowledge of the ending of the outflows.

subs.head: The fours: four foundations of mindfulness

blocks.text: "The mind is bound to the body by the bond of grasping; to feeling, by the bond of inward receiving; to the marks of objects, by discriminating; and to all these, by attachment." The four **foundations of mindfulness** (四念住) counter these four bonds: mindfulness of body, feeling, mind, and phenomena. Master Cháng Bǎi: a "bond" here is anything that restrains the mind, not necessarily an affliction; because the mind takes the body as itself, the body binds it.

quiz.q: What attainment does Venerable Miào Jìng say is needed for rebirth in the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Transformations?
options: one who has accomplished threshold concentration in the human world
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The Heaven of Mastery over Others' Transformations requires one who has accomplished threshold concentration in the human world." He adds, from his own seven-day recitation retreat, that such one-pointedness was only desire-realm concentration.

quiz.q: Among fully bound, not fully bound, and unbound, where does Venerable Miào Jìng place an ordinary being who has the eight absorptions?
options: not fully bound — desire-realm craving is gone, though afflictions of view remain
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Though this person is an ordinary being, having attained the four dhyānas and eight absorptions he has no bond of craving — desire-realm craving is gone, but afflictions of view remain." The reading note's "all ordinary beings are fully bound" disagrees.

quiz.q: The physical eye sees only exposed, unobstructed matter. How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe its limits?
options: it sees near but not far, front but not back, inside but not outside, day but not night, above but not below
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the physical eye "sees near but not far, front but not back, inside but not outside, day but not night, above but not below." These are spatial limits; the reading note's temporal "past or present" for the divine eye is not the lecture's point.

quiz.q: The treatise names three things by which one rests secure. What names does Venerable Miào Jìng give them?
options: emptiness, wishlessness, signlessness, and cessation are noble abidings; the four dhyānas, heavenly; the four immeasurables, Brahmā abidings
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: emptiness, wishlessness, signlessness, and cessation are the noble abidings; the four dhyānas are heavenly abidings; the four immeasurables are Brahmā abidings. Security must be inner; outwardly every place is alike.

quiz.q: The three true sagely silences counter non-Buddhists "who hold a silence vow." Who, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: the silence-observing ascetics, who do not speak
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: it is to eliminate the silence vow — the silence-observing ascetics who do not speak. The *Pixunji*: true sagely silence is the noble ones' tranquil action, also called silent action.

quiz.q: Per the treatise, by which bond is the mind bound to body, feeling, objects, and the rest?
options: to body by grasping, to feeling by receiving, to object-marks by discriminating, and to all these by attachment through greed and hatred
quiz.why: "Know that the mind is bound to the body by the bond of grasping; to feeling, by the bond of inward receiving; to the characteristic marks of form and other objects, by the bond of discriminating." The *Pixunji* pairs them with the four inversions.

quiz.q: Does Master Cháng Bǎi say each "bond" here is necessarily an afflictive bond?
options: not necessarily — whatever restrains the mind is a bond; since mind takes body as itself, body binds it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "What restrains a being's mind is called a bond — not necessarily of afflictive nature. Because the mind grasps the body as itself, the body binds this mind: bound by grasping." Only the fourth is expressly afflictive.
